title: Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids
seo_title: Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Class 12 Chemistry Worksheet (NCERT Ch 8)
standard_code: Class 12 Chemistry, Chapter 8: Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids
standard_text: Aldehydes and ketones: nomenclature, nature of carbonyl group, methods of preparation, physical and chemical properties, mechanism of nucleophilic addition, reactivity of alpha hydrogen in aldehydes, uses. Carboxylic acids: nomenclature, acidic nature, methods of preparation, physical and chemical properties, uses.
meta_desc: Free CBSE Class 12 Chemistry worksheets for NCERT Chapter 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids: naming carbonyl compounds, nucleophilic addition, tests, aldol and Cannizzaro reactions, acidity and esters. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Aldehydes reduce Tollens' and Fehling's reagents; ketones do not.
body_html:
How to think about it

Aldehydes and ketones contain the polar C=O group, which undergoes nucleophilic addition (HCN, NaHSO₃, ammonia derivatives). Aldehydes are more reactive than ketones and are oxidised by Tollens' and Fehling's reagents. Compounds with α-hydrogens undergo aldol condensation; those without undergo the Cannizzaro reaction.

Carboxylic acids are acidic because the carboxylate ion is resonance-stabilised; electron-withdrawing groups make them stronger. They form esters with alcohols, are reduced to alcohols by LiAlH₄ and give α-halo acids in the HVZ reaction.

Example

Ethanal + Tollens'?

aldehyde oxidised

Answer: silver mirror

Example

Strongest: CH₃COOH or Cl₃CCOOH?

three Cl

Answer: Cl₃CCOOH

Common mistakes

  • Saying ketones give a silver mirror.
  • Using NaBH₄ to reduce acids.
  • Giving the Cannizzaro reaction to ethanal.

faq.a: The carbonyl carbon of an aldehyde is less crowded and less shielded by electron-releasing alkyl groups.
